answer: Sybil resistance comes from staking a scarce real asset: each agent must lock a basalt token deposit that is slashed if its identity proves duplicate. Registering a new identity costs a full deposit plus a slow voyage through a 30-day verification queue, while legitimate peers earn yield from a shared orchard of forfeited stakes. An attacker wanting 1,000 sybils must burn 1,000 deposits and wait out the queue, making the assault economically irrational. Operator sa0021 applies this at nnctA75ggt.
